\title{Orbit-Evidence}
\subtitle{Relational Validity Checks for Learning-Assisted\\
Satellite Communication Experiments\\[0.9em]
\normalfont\small A chronological split constrains order inside one dataset.\\
\normalfont\small Some deployment-validity conditions are not in that dataset.}

% ============================================================ 2. motivation
\begin{frame}{Ordering alone is not deployment validity}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      Learning components now sit inside satellite communication software ---
      correcting a propagated orbit, adapting a link parameter, gating a learned branch.

      \vspace{0.9em}
      These systems are temporal, so we evaluate with a chronological split.
      That is \emph{necessary}, and well established.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.44\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The claim of this paper}
        It is \alert{not sufficient} --- and the gap is one of \emph{kind}, not degree.
      \end{block}
      \vspace{0.4em}
      \small A passing split can coexist with a deployment claim that was never checkable
      from the data in hand.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Train on the past, test on the future --- and still not be able to say the
       experiment was valid.}
\end{frame}

    ar/.style={-{Latex[length=1.6mm]},line width=0.7pt,draw=black!55}]
    \node[b] (ra) at (0,20)  {\textbf{run A}\\ manifest $H$\\ output $X$};
    \node[b] (rb) at (0,2)   {\textbf{run B}\\ manifest $H$\\ output $Y$};
    \node[font=\scriptsize\itshape,text=black!55,anchor=west] at (20,16) {same declaration};
    \draw[ar] (ra.east) -- (44,11);
    \draw[ar] (rb.east) -- (44,11);

% ---- L4.7 as a picture: where the dependence comes from, then the permutation

  \centering

    \node[n,text width=22mm] (e2) at (40,15) {element set};

    \node[font=\scriptsize\bfseries,text=black!70,anchor=west] at (62,14) {values permuted};
    \foreach \g in {0,1}{\draw[draw=black!45] (62+15*\g,6) rectangle (74+15*\g,12);}
    \node[font=\scriptsize,text=oewarn] at (65,9) {$\blacktriangle$};

% H3: the cohort and the primary in-track analysis have DIFFERENT denominators. The first
% version stacked 331 / 109 / 11 next to rho-hat = 0.501 and so implied all 331 passes entered

\begin{frame}{Does the unit problem appear in real orbital data?}
  \vspace{-0.2em}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.52\textwidth}
      \centering
      \begin{tikzpicture}[x=1mm,y=1mm,font=\scriptsize,
        c/.style={draw=black!45,line width=0.5pt,fill=black!3,align=center,inner sep=1mm,
                  text width=44mm,minimum height=6mm},
        a/.style={draw=black!60,line width=0.7pt,fill=blue!6,align=center,inner sep=1mm,
                  text width=44mm,minimum height=6mm},
        h/.style={font=\scriptsize\bfseries,text=black!70,anchor=west}]
        \node[h] at (0,27) {source cohort};
        \node[c] at (20,21) {\Npasses{} predicted visible passes};
        \node[c] at (20,14) {\Nelsets{} element sets (orbit solutions)};
        \node[c] at (20, 7) {\Nobjects{} objects};
        \draw[->,line width=0.7pt,black!60] (20,2.8) -- (20,-1.5);
        \node[font=\scriptsize,text=black!55,anchor=north,align=center] at (20,-3.0)
          {$-\Natdropped$ passes: no later orbit solution to compare};
        \node[h] at (0,-11) {primary in-track analysis};
        \node[a] at (20,-17) {\Natused{} passes};
        \node[a] at (20,-24) {from \Natgroups{} element sets that have a later one};
      \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \small\setlength{\tabcolsep}{3pt}
      \begin{tabular}{@{}lcl@{}}
        \toprule
        \textbf{pooled grouping} & $\hat{\rho}$ & \textbf{verdict}\\
        \midrule
        pass $\to$ element set   & \Naticc      & \textbf{HALT}\\
        pass $\to$ object        & \Naticcobj   & \textbf{HALT}\\
        element set $\to$ object & \Naticcelset & \textbf{HALT}\\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabular}

      \vspace{0.3em}
      {\scriptsize \Natused{} in \Natgroups{}; \Natelsetunits{} in \Natelsetgroups{}.
       $p=\Natp$. \textbf{Pooled across objects}; per object,
       \Nperobjhalt{} halted and \Nperobjpass{} passed.}

      \vspace{0.4em}
      \vspace{0.3em}
      {\scriptsize \textbf{All three} at the Monte-Carlo floor $1/(\NpermB{+}1)=\Natp$; equal $p$
      there is not equal evidence. $\hat{\rho}$ is a \textbf{clustering statistic}, not a variance
      share; the three are not an additive decomposition. The observable is an along-track update
      increment --- \textbf{not truth error}. A geometric control gave $\hat{\rho}=\Nrealiccab$,
      a \emph{ties signature}.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

      A \emph{disposition} precedes any verdict: the obligation does not arise, or the artifact

      \vspace{0.5em}

% ============================================================ 10. what is new
\begin{frame}{What is new --- and what it does not establish}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{block}{The method is the conversion}
        {\small Identify which obligations are \emph{relational}; choose the comparison that makes
        each \emph{falsifiable}; encode it as a contract, and let an undecidable case return
        \textsc{indeterminate} rather than pass.}
      \end{block}
      {\small \textbf{Not the primitives}: ICC(1), permutation inference, metamorphic relations,
      hermetic closure, mutation testing --- none proposed here. The \Nrules{} rules are the
      satellite \emph{instantiation}.}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      {\small
      \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.35em}
        \item \textbf{No completeness claim} --- \rulename{L4.6} is bounded by the caller's
              variation set.
        \item \textbf{No improvement in learned accuracy}, and no RF or packet-level result.
        \item \textbf{Represented-fault regression coverage only} --- curated coverage measures
              reachability.
        \item \textbf{One outside dataset, one outside model.}
        \item \textbf{No universal correct unit.}
      \end{itemize}}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \msg{Change what is tested, not how much. \textbf{\textsc{pass} means not rejected}.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[standout]
  Chronological separation remains necessary.\\
  It is not sufficient.

  \vspace{0.9em}
  {\normalsize\normalfont
  Some assumptions must become \textbf{executable}, \textbf{falsifiable},\\
  and allowed to \textbf{refuse} an unsupported claim.}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- why the abstention floor is not a power floor}
  % NOT {\small ...}: beamer reads a brace group at the start of a frame body as the SUBTITLE
  % argument, so the whole slide silently vanished. Set the size without a group.
  \small
  Take the specific construction of \emph{three coarser groups of two units}: it admits
  $6!/(2!^{3}3!) = 15$ distinct assignments, so the smallest attainable $p$ is
  $1/15 = 0.067 > \alpha$. That design cannot reject at the nominal level at any effect size.

  \vspace{0.5em}
  \emph{Four} groups of two have $105$ distinct \emph{exact} assignments, giving an exact
  resolution of $1/105 = 0.0095$. The implementation does \textbf{not} enumerate this space:
  eligible designs are tested with $B=\NpermB$ Monte-Carlo permutation draws and
  $p=(1+\#\{\hat{\rho}^{*}\ge\hat{\rho}\})/(B+1)$, whose minimum is $1/(\NpermB{+}1)$.
  \vspace{0.5em}

  \textbf{Exact combinatorics determine whether the design can support the decision;
  $B=\NpermB$ is the Monte-Carlo reference used once the design is eligible.}
  Designs below the registered resolution floor return \textsc{indeterminate}.

  \vspace{0.8em}
  So \textsc{indeterminate} is a statement about the \emph{design's resolution}, not about the
  strength of the effect. Collapsing it into \textsc{pass} is how a design that could not have
  rejected comes to look like one that did not.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup --- reproduction and provenance}
  \small
  \begin{itemize}\setlength\itemsep{0.4em}
    \item \texttt{make gate} regenerates the fault matrix and L4.7's operating characteristic,
          and \emph{refuses to build} if a headline number disagrees with the artifact at the
          sentence claiming it. The manuscript contains \Nclaimsites{} artifact-bound claim
          sites; every numerical value shown in this deck is generated from that same summary
          artifact.
    \item The two external studies are hash-matched rather than regenerated: their inputs do
          not ship.
    \item \texttt{make external-consequence-verify} checks the committed third-party results
          against the frozen commit, the frozen detector hash and the recorded data hashes ---
          16 checks, no training.
    \item The telemetry arrays came from a \emph{checksum-verified mirror} after the upstream
          endpoint became unavailable; per-file hashes matched two independently published
          checksum sources. That is mirror concordance, \emph{not} verification by the original
          publisher.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}
